Appeal No. 19/2023 In The Court Of Ms. Smita Garg, Special Judge (Pc Act) (Cbi)-13, Rouse Avenue District Court, New Delhi Cnr No. Dlct11-000825-2023 Crl. Appeal No. 19/2023 In the matter of: Central Bureau of Investigation Through: Sh. Piyush Sharma Inspector of Police, Cbi, Eo-I, New Delhi, 5-B, Cgo Complex 3rd Floor, New Delhi ..... Appellant Versus 1. Sh. Praveen Garg R/o 3/26, East Punjabi Bagh, New Delhi-110026 2. Sh. Mukesh Goel R/o Ag-215, Shalimar Bagh, New Delhi-110088 .....Respondents Date of institution of the appeal : 30.11.2023 Date of conclusion of arguments : 12.11.2025 Date of pronouncement of judgment : 06.12.2025 Cbi v. Praveen Garg & Anr. Page No. 1 of 26 Crl. Appeal No. 19/2023 Judgment:
texts.facts: The brief background relevant for the disposal of the appeal is as under: 2.1. On 31.05.2011, CBI filed the chargesheet for the commission of the offence punishable under Section 120B IPC read with Section 3 & 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 against the respondents herein and one Smt. Sushila Rani, who was the proprietor of M/s. Lakra Oil Trading Company. 2.2. By way of the Dealership Agreement dated 25.01.1990, M/s. Lakra Oil Trading Company had been appointed as the dealer of M/s. Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (for short 'BPCL') in respect of the petroleum products namely Light CBI v. Praveen Garg & Anr. Page No. 2 of 26 Diesel Oil and Superior Kerosene Oil. As per the charge sheet, the firm was also the authorized dealer of Furnace Oil. 2.3. M/s. Lakra Oil Trading Company was also having the Kerosene License No. 3614/19 dated 20.02.1990 issued by the Food and Supply Department, Govt. of NCT of Delhi to procure the kerosene oil from BPCL and supply it to the kerosene oil depots under the public distribution system. As per the prevalent practice and the terms of license, no licensee was authorized to store/decant any quantity of kerosene oil meant for the kerosene oil depots at any place before its delivery and was required to submit the acknowledgment/compliance report of delivery to the concerned kerosene oil depots within 36 hours. 2.4. In nutshell, it was alleged in the charge-sheet that despite having the dealership of Light Diesel Oil and Superior Kerosene Oil only, Smt. Sushila Rani in conspiracy with the respondents used to store High Speed Diesel in contravention of Section 2 (f) read with Section 3 of the Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply, Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005. Apart from High Speed Diesel, they were also unauthorizedly storing kerosene oil and CBS Haldia. Further, they used to bring blue colour kerosene oil of public CBI v. Praveen Garg & Anr. Page No. 3 of 26 distribution system meant for kerosene oil depots to the premises of M/s. Lakra Oil Trading Company and after decolouring it with the help of bleaching powder and other chemicals, used to mix the same with other standard petroleum products and sell the adulterated petroleum products to different companies and factories in contravention of Section 3 read with Section 4 of the Kerosene (Restriction on Use and Fixation of Ceiling Price) Order, 1993 and the Delhi Kerosene Oil (Export and Price) Control Order, 1962. 2.5. According to the prosecution, upon receipt of source information, a surprise check was conducted on 12.05.2010 by a team comprising of CBI Officials, Officers of BPCL and an independent witness at the premises of M/s. Lakra Oil Trading Company located at Site No. 1, Block-8, Geeta Colony, Delhi. During the surprise check, following petroleum products and adulterants were found at the premises: Cbi vs Sh.Praveen Garg And Anr on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95741817/ 2 1 Kerosene oil in underground tank 5,000 Ltrs 2 Light Diesel Oil in underground tank 20,000 Ltrs 3 CBS Haldia in underground tank 30,000 Ltrs 4 High Speed Diesel in underground tank 5,000 Ltrs CBI v. Praveen Garg & Anr. Page No. 4 of 26 5 Bleached Kerosene oil in Syntex tank 1,500 Lrts 6 Hydrogen Peroxide in plastic cane 50 Ltrs. 7 Unknown chemical in plastic cane 50 Ltrs. 8 Bleaching powder 2 bags 9 Barrels containing diesel 8 nos. 10 Barrels containing black oil 22 nos. 11 Barrels containing kerosene oil 2 nos. 2.6. Based on visual observation and density checking, Sh. K.G. Ghatwai, Senior Manager, Quality Control Cell, BPCL, who was a member of the team, informed that the petroleum products contained in all the four underground tanks and the Syntex tank appeared to be adulterated. Thus, samples from the underground tanks as well as the Syntex tank were drawn and sealed in the presence of the independent witness Sh. Ashok Kumar Aggarwal. Samples of Hydrogen Peroxide and unknown chemical found at the premises were also taken. Out of three sets of samples of seven products, one set of samples was given to Sh. K.G. Ghatwai and second set of samples was retained by the CBI Officers. At the time of inspection, three employees of M/s. Lakra Oil Trading Company namely Sh. Virender Kumar, CBI v. Praveen Garg & Anr. Page No. 5 of 26 Sh. Giriraj Kumar and Sh. Suraj were found present at the premises and they informed that they were working for Sh. Praveen Garg (the respondent no.1). Since the respondent no.1 failed to join the surprise check, third set of samples was handed over to the representative/employee of the firm namely Sh. Giriraj. Videography of the premises was also carried out by the technical team of CBI. 2.7. FIR bearing RC No. 0722010(E)0004/2010 was registered on 12.05.2010. The respondent no.1 was arrested on 13.05.2010. During his custodial interrogation, it transpired that in or around the year 2006, the respondent no.1 had taken over the business of M/s. Lakra Oil Trading Company from its proprietor Smt. Sushila Rani on account of her old age and that he had got executed a General Power of Attorney dated 01.08.2006 in favour of his brother in law Sh. Mukesh Goel (respondent no.2) authorizing him to manage the business affairs of the firm for which the respondent no.1 used to pay an amount of Rs.15,000/- per month to Smt. Sushila Rani. 2.8. During investigation, Smt. Sushila Rani maintained that though she is the proprietor of M/s. Lakra Oil Trading Company but she had handed over the business affairs of the firm to both the CBI v. Praveen Garg & Anr. Page No. 6 of 26 respondents. She also produced the attested photocopy of General Power of Attorney dated 01.08.2006 executed by her in favour of the respondent no.2. However, investigation revealed that she was actively involved in the affairs of the firm along with the respondents and had also signed the inspection report dated 30.04.2010 conducted by the Cbi vs Sh.Praveen Garg And Anr on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95741817/ 3 officials of BPCL. 2.9. The samples of the products collected during the surprise check on 12.05.2010 were got analyzed from Quality Control Laboratory of BPCL. Sample test reports dated 20.05.2010 confirmed adulteration as the samples failed to meet the standard specifications of the petroleum products. The petroleum products seized were thus confiscated vide order dated 25.08.2010 of the Deputy Commissioner/Collector, East District, Delhi and pursuant to the said order, BPCL evacuated the entire confiscated petroleum products from the premises of M/s. Lakra Oil Trading Company between 15.10.2010 to 21.10.2010. 2.10. On the basis of material produced with the chargesheet, cognizance of the offence punishable under Section 120B IPC read with Sections 3 & 7 of Essential Commodities Act was taken on 28.06.2011 and the respondents as well as Smt. Sushila CBI v. Praveen Garg & Anr. Page No. 7 of 26 Rani were summoned by the Ld. Trial Court. Vide order 07.01.2013, charge for the commission of the abovesaid offence was directed to be framed against them. Formal charge was framed on 11.01.2013. However, Smt. Sushila Rani preferred Criminal Revision Petition No. 04/2013 against the order on charge before the Ld. Sessions Court. Vide order dated 05.06.2013, the said revision petition was allowed and the Ld. Sessions Court discharged Smt. Sushila Rani by observing that after the execution of General Power of Attorney dated 01.08.2006, she had no concern with the day to day affairs of the firm. Order dated 05.06.2013 was not challenged by the CBI and has attained finality. 2.11. During the course of trial, CBI examined 31 witnesses. Statements of the respondents under Section 313 CrPC were recorded on 14.02.2023 wherein they denied the allegations against them and claimed innocence. However, they chose not to lead evidence in their defence. Aggrieved therefrom, CBI has preferred the instant appeal before this Court.

ARGUMENTS ADVANCED ON BEHALF OF CBI: Cbi vs Sh.Praveen Garg And Anr on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95741817/ 4 4. Senior PP for CBI has assailed the impugned judgment by contending that the Ld. Trial Court had failed to appreciate the evidence available on record. He has submitted that PW-3 Sh. Suraj, who was the employee of M/s. Lakra Oil Trading Company, had categorically deposed that the respondent no. 2 Sh. Mukesh Goel was the owner of the said firm. He has submitted that the customers of the said firm had also deposed that they used to deal with the respondents for purchase of CBI v. Praveen Garg & Anr. Page No. 9 of 26 furnace oil from the firm. He has submitted that it is also the matter of record that the respondent no. 2 Sh. Mukesh Goel had got released the articles such as motor-pumps etc. on superdari in the capacity of authorized representative of the firm. He has argued that the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that the above material was sufficient to prove that the respondents were managing the affairs of the firm and thus, mere non-production of the original General Power of Attorney dated 01.08.2006 executed by Smt. Sushila Rani in favour of Sh. Mukesh Goel (respondent no.2) could not have been deemed as fatal to the case of the prosecution. 5. He has also submitted that during the surprise check conducted on 12.05.2010, huge quantities of unauthorized petroleum products including High Speed Diesel and Kerosene oil and adulterants were found at the premises of the firm. He has submitted that as per the test reports dated 20.05.2010 of the Quality Control Laboratory of BPCL, the samples of the petroleum products collected from the premises did not conform to the standard specifications. He has argued that since the said laboratory is approved by Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and is also accredited by National Accreditation Board for testing and Calibration Laboratories, the doubt expressed by the CBI v. Praveen Garg & Anr. Page No. 10 of 26 Ld. Trial Court on the correctness of the test reports by observing that the samples ought to have been sent to some other independent laboratory was unwarranted. He has contended that in view of the recovery of the unauthorized petroleum products and the adulterants coupled with the opinion given in the test reports, the prosecution had succeeded in proving its case that the respondents were indulging in the process of adulteration. 6. He has further submitted that unauthorized possession of High Speed Diesel and Kerosene oil by the respondents was in contravention of Section 2 (f) read with Section 3(6) of the Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply, Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005 and Kerosene (Restriction on Use and Fixation of Ceiling Price) Order, 1993 respectively for which they were liable to be convicted under Section 3 read with Section 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955. 7. Senior PP for CBI has urged that though the order of acquittal is not ordinarily interfered with but since the reasonings and findings returned by the Ld. Trial Court are perverse, the impugned judgment deserves to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. In support of his CBI v. Praveen Garg & Anr. Page No. 11 of 26 submission, he placed reliance on State of Punjab v. Karnail Singh, AIR 2003 SC 3609; Kamaljit Singh v. State of Punjab, AIR 2004 SC 69; Arun Kumar and Ors v. State of U.P, AIR 1989 SC 1445; and State of UP v. Satish, AIR 2005 SC 1000. ARGUMENTS ADVANCED ON BEHALF OF RESPONDENTS: Cbi vs Sh.Praveen Garg And Anr on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95741817/ 5 8. On the other hand, the counsel for the respondent has submitted that after meticulously evaluating the evidence available on record, Ld. Trial Court has passed a well-reasoned judgment thereby acquitting the respondents of the charges against them. He has submitted that the judgment of acquittal can be interfered with only if the appellate court, after re-appreciating the evidence, is satisfied that the only possible conclusion was that the guilt of the accused had been established beyond the reasonable doubt and that the order of acquittal is perverse but the order of acquittal cannot be overturned only on the ground that a view other than the view taken by the trial court is possible. In support of his argument, the counsel for the respondents placed reliance on Bhupatbhai Bachubhai Chavda & Anr. v. State of Gujarat (2024) 4 SCR 322 and State of Madhya Pradesh v. Ramveer Singh, 2025 INSC 952. 9. He has submitted that Smt. Sushila Rani, who was the CBI v. Praveen Garg & Anr. Page No. 12 of 26 proprietor of M/s. Lakra Oil Trading Company, was the authorized dealer of BPCL and in view of the terms and conditions of the Dealership Agreement dated 25.01.1990, she could not have transferred the dealership or the kerosene license to any other person including the respondents. He has submitted that the prime document on which the prosecution had relied to show the involvement of the respondents was the General Power of Attorney dated 01.08.2006 alleged to have been executed by Smt. Sushila Rani in favour of the respondent no.2 but neither the original General Power of Attorney dated 01.08.2006 was produced on record nor its due execution had been proved by the prosecution. He has submitted that since the prosecution had failed to lead any reliable evidence to prove that the business of M/s. Lakra Oil Trading Company had been taken over by the respondents, the Ld. Trial Court was justified in opining that Smt. Sushila Rani alone was responsible for the violation, if any, of the Control Orders and that the respondents cannot be held liable for the same. He has argued that since the CBI has failed to point out any perversity or illegality in the impugned judgment, the appeal deserves to be dismissed. ANALYSIS AND DISCUSSION: 10. On 11.01.2013, the Ld. Trial Court had framed the following CBI v. Praveen Garg & Anr. Page No. 13 of 26 charge against the respondents and Smt. Sushila Rani: "That on or before 12.05.2010, at premises of M/s Lakra Oil Trading Company at site no.1, Block-8, Geeta Colony, Delhi, you all accused entered into a criminal conspiracy for adulteration, storage and unauthorized sale of petroleum products in contravention to dealership agreement in favour of M/s Lakra Trading Oil Company and committed malpractice within the meaning of Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel Regulation of Supply (Distribution and Prevention of Malpractice) Order 2005 and violated the provisions of said order as well as Section 3 r/w Section 4 of Kerosene (Restriction of Use and Fixation of Ceiling Price) Order 1993 and Delhi Kerosene Oil (Export & Price) Control Order 1962 and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 3 and 7 of Essential Commodities Act read with Section 120B IPC and within my cognizance." Cbi vs Sh.Praveen Garg And Anr on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95741817/ 6 Section 2 (f) of the Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply, Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005 defines 'Malpractices'. It inter alia includes unauthorized possession and adulteration of High Speed Diesel. Section 3 (6) of the said Order provides that no dealer, transporter, consumer or any other person shall indulge in any manner in any one or more of the malpractices. 12. Section 3 (2) of the Kerosene (Restriction on Use and Fixation of Ceiling Price) Order, 1993 provides that no dealer appointed under the public distribution system or a transporter shall sell, distribute or supply kerosene oil under the public distribution system to any person other than the person to whom the supplies are meant for. Section 4 of the said Order is not applicable to the facts of the present case but for ready reference, the same has been reproduced as under: "4. Procurement, storage and sale of kerosene under the public distribution system:- (1) No dealer having stocks of kerosene supplied under the public distribution system at the business premises, including the place of storage:- (a) shall unless otherwise directed by the Government or CBI v. Praveen Garg & Anr. Page No. 15 of 26 Government Oil Company, refuse to sell, distribute or supply the kerosene to any consumer on any working day, during working hours, (b) shall keep his business premises, including the place of storage closed during working hours on any working day without the prior written permission of the Government or the Government Oil Company, (c) shall sell, distribute or supply kerosene at a price higher than that fixed by the Government or Government Oil Company. (2) Every dealer appointed under the public distribution system shall take all reasonable steps to ensure that adequate stocks of kerosene are available at the business premises including the place of storage at all times. Explanation-for the purpose of sub-clauses (1) (1) the expression "working hours" means the working hour fixed by the concerned Oil Company in accordance with the Shops and Establishments Act in force in the respective State or Union Territory." 13. 17. Sr. PP for CBI has contended that the Ld. Trial Court erred in discarding the GPA and failed to appreciate that the copy thereof had been seized on its production by Smt. Sushila Rani and thus, the execution of GPA was not in dispute.
